small_guidance:
- The conv (128×64×128×128 with 3×3) dominates runtime; the instance-norm kernel is already trivial. Further tuning of the IN kernel won't move the needle. If staying small, reduce IN launch overhead by widening BLOCK only when needed and dropping num_warps=32 config (16K elements / 32 warps = poor occupancy on 4090).
- Consider channels-last layout for the conv output so the IN kernel can coalesce loads along HW contiguously (already contiguous now, so minor).
- Add num_stages=3 and num_warps=4 configs for the IN kernel autotune key on HW; current configs are all very wide.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with BLOCK_M/N/K around 64/128/32, channels-last input layout so the GEMM-K (IC*kh*kw) dimension is contiguous. This is where the headroom is — conv is >90% of runtime.
- Fuse the instance-norm into a two-pass design over the conv output: pass 1 = conv-GEMM kernel writing per-(N,OC) partial sum and sum-of-squares into a small workspace; pass 2 = a single elementwise kernel that reads workspace, computes mean/rstd, and applies `(y - mean) * rstd / divide_by` while writing the final output. This avoids a separate IN pass over the full 128×128×126×126 tensor.
- Alternatively, since output spatial (126*126 = 15876) is large per (N,C), keep conv as its own kernel but make it write directly in channels-last and have the IN kernel issue one program per (N,C) reading a strided column — pick whichever layout makes the conv epilogue cheapest.
